summary: Compress the intro and preamble to make room. Add rules for: 以Y为目的 as identity-91 (have-purpose-91 only for purpose clauses); parenthetical identity-91 clauses; 是 Adj as have-mod-91; 等 as last :opN, :example lists, 有-03 with (and A B); control-verb subject re-entrancy and shared contrast time; aspect fixes (nominal under aspectual verb = process, exist/survive = state, past speech act = performance); speaker as conceiver of all reported content plus :quote; no links for nodes without aspect; individual-person for characters, planet NEs; consecutive for 后来, no node for discourse 就; same-sentence short-form coref; marriage titles.

edits.old:
You annotate a whole document in Uniform Meaning Representation (UMR): every sentence's sentence-level
graph, then all the document-level relations (temporal, modal, coreference) of the document. The document
is under **Input** at the end, one sentence per line.

**Make the annotation as correct as you can.** It is compared, node by node and relation by relation,
with an expert gold annotation made by these guidelines, so every concept, sense, role, attribute value
and document-level relation counts. Take the time this needs:

- Read the guidelines below carefully before you start, and go back to them for every decision you are
  not sure of: the concept and its sense, the numbered and non-core roles, abstract concepts and named
  entities, aspect, modal strength, polarity, and the temporal, modal and coreference relations.
- Follow the examples: when a sentence has a construction an example shows, annotate it the way the
  example does.
- Do not guess when you can check: use the three tools (see Tools): search the full guidelines with
  `search_guidelines` whenever the guidelines above do not settle a case, look up every predicate in
  PropBank with `propbank_lookup` before you choose its sense and numbered roles, and look up how the gold
  data annotates a construction, a word or a relation with `search_annotations`. Call them as often as you
  need: many calls are expected.
- Before you go on to the next sentence, check the graph against the guidelines once more: every word
  that carries meaning has its concept, every event its aspect, every role the right direction; and at
  the end check that the document-level relations cover every event and entity the guidelines ask for.
edits.new:
You annotate a whole document (under **Input**, one sentence per line) in Uniform Meaning Representation (UMR):
every sentence's graph, then the document-level temporal, modal and coreference relations. It is compared node by
node and relation by relation with an expert gold annotation made by these guidelines; every concept, sense, role,
attribute and relation counts.

- Follow the guidelines and their examples. When they do not settle a case, use `search_guidelines`; look up every
  predicate with `propbank_lookup` before choosing its sense and roles; check gold constructions with
  `search_annotations`. Many calls are expected.
- Before the next sentence, check the graph: every meaningful word has its concept, every event its aspect, every
  role the right direction; at the end check the document-level relations cover every event and entity.

edits.old:
A short version of the UMR 0.9 specification (`umr_guidelines.md` in this folder, umr4nlp/umr-guidelines),
for annotating Chinese and English at Stage 1 (numbered PropBank roles). It keeps what an annotator needs for
most sentences and leaves out the typological material, the fine-grained lattices, the field-linguistics
sections and most of the examples. Where the full guideline uses the older short names (`AUTH`, `DCT`,
`FullAff`, `:modstr`, `:ref-person`, `Performance`), this version uses the names of the UMR release data
(`author`, `document-creation-time`, `full-affirmative`, `:modal-strength`, `:refer-person`, `performance`).

edits.old:
Finer values (`inceptive`, `directed-activity`, `semelfactive`, ...) exist in the full guideline; use them
only when they are clear.
- Annotate event–event relations only when they are clear.
- Channel nouns (TV, radio, network) modifying a noun are `:medium`; places are `:place`; no `:wiki` in Chinese.
or a clause has a marked purpose clause (为了, 以, 以便)
edits.new: or a clause has a marked purpose clause (为了, 以便)

edits.text:
- A purpose stated as a noun (以 Y 为目的/目标) is `(i / identity-91 :ARG1 (m / 目的 :purpose-of <event>) :ARG2 Y)`; Y is a plain concept without aspect or links.
- A parenthetical or colon restatement (slogan, gloss) is its own `identity-91 :ARG1 <noun> :ARG2 <content>` clause joined to the previous clause by `and`, never `:medium`/`:mod`.
- 后来/*later, then* joining two predicates → `(c / consecutive :op1 … :op2 …)`, no node for 后来. Discourse 就/便 outside a condition gets no node.

X 是 Adj (的) / X 都是 Adj: `have-mod-91 :ARG1 X :ARG2 Adj` (adverb as `:mod` of have-mod-91), never an `Adj-01` event. A title held through marriage (first lady) is `have-rel-role-91 :ARG3 <title>`, country `:place` and former `:mod` on the title.

等/*etc.* closing a list is its last `:opN`. "N 有 A、B…等" listing examples of N → `:example (and …)` on N, no 有 node; "A 与 B 有 <relation noun>" → `有-03 :ARG0 (and A B) :ARG1 <noun>`, never `:companion`;

- Exception (control): the subject of an aspectual or control verb (继续, 停止, 开始) is its `:ARG0` and re-enters as `:ARG0` of its event complement, event nominals included. A time expression scoping over both clauses of a but-91/contrast attaches to both clause events.

edits.old: → `habitual`, also for a process nominal naming such a practice
edits.new: → `habitual`, also for a process nominal naming such a practice (but an event-nominal complement of an aspectual verb such as 停止 is `process`)

edits.old: State verbs (have, own, belong, be; 有, 拥有, 是)
edits.new: State verbs (have, own, belong, be, exist, survive; 有, 拥有, 是, 存在, 生存)

edits.old: Also: a purpose or intended action is `activity`;
edits.new: Also: a completed past speech act (claim, announce; 宣称) is `performance`; a purpose or intended action is `activity`;

edits.text: Every event of the reported content, including an appended slogan or quotation and later clauses still reporting it, takes the speaker as modal parent; the content's top node carries `:quote <saying verb>`.

- any node without `:aspect` (plain concepts, list items, locatives); these get no modal parent either.
  Do not link a habitual relative-clause event to a past performance.
So is a named character, human or not (a species word before the name is its first `:opN`); a planet name is a `planet` named entity.
